vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: parallel
Version: 1.0.7

The skill is classified as suspicious due to a critical shell injection vulnerability found in `scripts/parallel.sh`. This bash script directly embeds user-controlled input (e.g., `$input`, `$processor`) into a `curl -d` JSON payload without proper sanitization, allowing for arbitrary command execution on the agent's host. For example, a crafted query could execute `$(id)` or `$(rm -rf /)` via the `research`, `company`, or `person` commands. While the Python scripts appear benign and use safer argument parsing, the `parallel.sh` script presents a severe Remote Code Execution (RCE) risk.

llm.summary: The skill's code, runtime instructions, and requested environment variables are consistent with a Parallel.ai web-research client and do not request unrelated credentials or unusual installs.

dimensions.detail: Name/description align with the included scripts and declared requirements. The single required credential (PARALLEL_API_KEY) is used throughout to call Parallel.ai endpoints; required binaries (python3, curl, jq) are actually used by the scripts.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and scripts only perform API calls to Parallel.ai (and optionally to browser-use.com for authenticated browsing) and local formatting; they do not read unrelated system files or request unrelated environment variables. Note: monitor creation supports user-provided webhook URLs (which will receive data from the service) and authenticated browsing uses an optional BROWSERUSE_API_KEY — these are expected features but can transmit queried content to external endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No opaque install/downloads. SKILL.md recommends pip-installing 'parallel-sdk' and 'requests' from PyPI (standard practice). The package is instruction/code-only with no remote archive extraction or URL-shortened downloads.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only PARALLEL_API_KEY is required (declared as primary credential) and is used by all scripts. BROWSERUSE_API_KEY is optional and documented for authenticated page access. No unrelated secrets or multiple unrelated credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill is not always-on (always: false) and does not modify other skills or system-wide settings. It is user-invocable; disable-model-invocation is set, so it will not be autonomously invoked by the model (limiting blast radius).
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a straightforward client for Parallel.ai. Before installing: 1) Only provide a PARALLEL_API_KEY you obtained from platform.parallel.ai; treat it like any API secret. 2) Avoid including sensitive personal/company data in queries because the skill sends your queries/content to Parallel.ai and (if enabled) to browser-use.com for authenticated browsing or to any webhook URLs you supply. 3) The monitor feature can post events to arbitrary webhook URLs you provide — only use endpoints you control or trust. 4) The optional BROWSERUSE_API_KEY grants the skill the ability to fetch authenticated pages; only set it if you understand and trust that provider. 5) Be mindful of cost/usage (generators/pro tiers, monitor cadences). If you have any doubt about the vendor, verify the API host and keys out-of-band and consider creating a scoped/limited API key or using a dedicated account whose compromise would have limited impact.
